title: Platform systems & services: how-tos, dashboards & alerts, runbooks, retrospective, and Q3 roadmap
author: Samir Patel
body:
Purpose:

This page consolidates the Platform team’s canonical guidance for systems & services ownership, operational how-tos, dashboard and alert standards, an exemplar runbook, key retrospective findings from Q2 2026, and the Q3 2026 roadmap. Use this as the single source of truth for on-call run actions, dashboard construction, alert tuning, and near-term platform priorities.

Scope:

- Applies to all Platform-managed services (platform-api, routing-proxy, telemetry-ingest, kgc-cache, infra-ops).
- Intended audience: SREs, Platform Engineers, Release Engineers, and Engineering Managers.
- Not a replacement for service-specific runbooks; link service-specific pages from the inventory table below.

1) Inventory: systems & services (owner, SLO, primary dashboard)

| Service name | Primary owner | SLO (p99 latency / availability) | Primary dashboard |
|--------------|---------------|----------------------------------|------------------|
| platform-api | platform-team | p99 <= 120ms / 99.95%            | /dashboards/platform-api-main |
| routing-proxy | infra-team   | p99 <= 30ms / 99.9%              | /dashboards/routing-proxy-ops |
| telemetry-ingest | observability | p99 <= 200ms / 99.8%        | /dashboards/telemetry-ingest |
| kgc-cache    | serving-runtime | p99 <= 18ms / 99.9%           | /dashboards/kgc-cache-hitrates |
| infra-ops    | platform-ops  | N/A (operational)               | /dashboards/infra-ops-overview |

2) Dashboard & alert standards (why and how)

Summary: Dashboards are for situational awareness and troubleshooting; alerts are for actionable paging where a human must intervene. Follow these rules: 

- Dashboard naming: team-service-purpose (e.g., platform-api-main, platform-api-latency-detail).
- Dashboard layout: top row = global SLO tiles, second row = latency & error heatmaps, third row = resource metrics (CPU/GPU/memory), fourth row = dependency panels (DB/cache/third-party).
- Chart conventions: use p50/p95/p99 lines for latency; show request rate and error rate on shared x-axis.
- Retention & resolution: dashboards in Grafana, 90-day default retention for business metrics; 7-day default for high-cardinality debug logs.

Alerting principles:

- Only alert on symptoms where human action is expected (failures impacting customers or SLOs).
- Prefer longer, stable signals for paging (e.g., sustained p99 breach for 3m) and shorter signals for Slack-only noisy indicators.
- Each alert must include: description, impact, runbook link, escalation policy, and suggested mitigation steps.

Standard alert categories and examples:

- SLO breaches (page): p99 latency > SLO for 5m OR availability < target for 3m.
- Resource saturation (page): node CPU > 90% for 10m, GPU memory pressure > 88% for 5m.
- Service errors (page): 5xx rate > 1% of requests sustained for 3m (service-specific baseline applies).
- Dependency failures (page): DB connection errors > 0.5% for 5m or cache miss storm causing latency spikes.
- Non-pager (Slack only): queue depth > warning threshold, small transient spikes in telemetry ingestion.

Alert payload template (copy into Alertmanager/Grafana):

"""
Alert: {{ alert_name }}
Severity: {{ severity }}
Impact: {{ short impact summary }}
Symptoms: {{ key metrics and query }}
Runbook: https://confluence.internal/eng-platform/runbooks/{{ service }}
Pages: on-call-platform -> secondary on-call -> eng manager (escalation intervals 10m, 20m)
"""

3) How-tos (common procedures)

A. Deploy a dashboard change (Grafana):

1. Branch: create feature branch in grafana-dashboards repo (naming: dashboard/<service>/<short-desc>).
2. Schema: use panel templates and variables from /repos/grafana-dashboards/README.md.
3. Local preview: run docker-compose -f preview.yml up and open http://localhost:3000.
4. PR: include screenshot, short testing notes, and which SLOs are impacted (if any).
5. Review: assign to owner and observability-reviewer.
6. Merge: merge to main triggers CI that pushes to staging Grafana.
7. Promote: stage -> prod using the promotion job in CI (requires two approvals for prod).

B. Tune an alert to reduce noise:

1. Confirm signal: correlate alert with dashboard, logs (Loki) and traces (Tempo).
2. Validate impact: query historical rate to see false-positive window.
3. Adjust window/threshold: prefer increasing duration or moving to slack-only for a 30-day trial.
4. Annotate alert: add a note with rationale, who approved, and expected review date.

C. Add a new monitored service to platform monitoring:

1. Create service entry in monitoring-registry.yml: name, owner, SLO, prometheus job name, alert contacts.
2. Onboard metrics: ensure metrics follow labels: service, instance, environment, shard.
3. Add baseline dashboards: use service-dashboard template and populate panel queries.
4. Define alerts: SLO-based and dependency alerts; add to Alertmanager routing.
5. Run a 72-hour validation window in staging and collect feedback from on-call.

4) Runbook: platform-api high-latency (exemplar)

Title: platform-api p99 latency breach
Severity: P1 (page) if sustained > SLO for 5m or > 2x SLO for 1m
Owners: platform on-call -> platform senior SRE -> platform eng manager
Runbook link: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-api-p99-latency

Immediate steps (first 10 minutes):

1. Acknowledge page and post status in #oncall-platform (include paging link).
2. Check primary dashboard (platform-api-main): p50/p95/p99, RPS, errors, and downstream latencies.
3. Is error rate elevated? If yes, collect top error types (status codes, stack traces) and consider immediate rollback of recent deploy.
4. If errors are low but latency high, check cache hitrates (kgc-cache), DB latency, and routing-proxy p99.
5. Scale up: if CPU/GPU saturation visible and autoscaler has headroom, trigger manual scale up via platform autoscale playbook (CLI: platformctl scale service platform-api --count +2).

Diagnostic commands and queries (examples):

- Prometheus: rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="platform-api"}[5m])
- Logs (Loki): {job="platform-api"} | json | count_over_time({job="platform-api"}[5m])
- Traces (Tempo): search for slow spans with tag service=platform-api

Mitigation checklist (if initial steps don’t resolve):

- Rollback candidate: identify last successful tag and initiate rollback via release pipeline.
- Circuit-break: reduce traffic to non-critical routes with routing policy (playbook: routing-proxy/circuit-break.md).
- Fallback: route to compatible model variants or degraded code path for heavy endpoints.

Post-incident:

- Run retrospective within 72 hours. Capture timeline, mitigation actions, root cause hypothesis, and three follow-up tasks (owner + ETA).
- If SLO impacted, follow SRE SLO remediation process (notify product, update status page).

5) Retrospective (Q2 2026 highlights and action items)

Summary: Q2 saw two customer-impacting incidents: (1) telemetry-ingest backlog causing delayed metrics ingestion (Impact: 4 hours, root cause: backpressure misconfiguration), and (2) a routing-proxy misconfiguration during a canary rollout causing elevated p99 for platform-api (Impact: 45 minutes).

Root causes and learnings:

- Over-reliance on optimistic autoscaler defaults — we must codify conservative buffer settings for bursty workloads.
- Canary rollout validation gaps — promote staging canary validation steps to include realistic traffic with KV cache warmups.
- Alert tuning: two alerts fired repeatedly as false positives; moved to Slack-only after SRE review.

Action items (owners and target dates):

1. Autoscaler conservative profile (owner: infra-team, ETA: 2026-08-15).
2. Canary validation harness (owner: release-engineering, ETA: 2026-09-01).
3. Monitoring playbook for telemetry-ingest (owner: observability, ETA: 2026-08-05).
3. Alert hygiene sweep across platform services (owner: platform-ops, ETA: 2026-08-10).

6) Q3 2026 Roadmap (prioritized)

- M1 (Aug-Sep): Implement autoscaler conservative profiles and ship default safe profiles for latency-sensitive services.
- M2 (Sep): Canary validation harness with synthetic KV warmups and golden traffic replay.
- M3 (Sept-Oct): Grafana dashboard refactor project — standardize panel templates and reduce duplication.
- M4 (Oct): SLO observability improvements — add automated SLO regression detection and weekly SLO health digest to #slo-health.

Success metrics for Q3:

- Reduce P1 incidents from platform by 30% vs Q2.
- Decrease median time to mitigation (MTTM) for platform-api incidents by 25%.
- Reduce alert noise: decrease alerts that page on <25% actionable rate by 50%.

- Pager rotation: PagerDuty schedule: platform-rotation
- Access: Grafana (SSO + SAML), Prometheus (read-only via SSO; write via service account), Alertmanager configs in git (protected branch).

9) Change log

- 2026-07-10: Document created (Samir Patel).
- 2026-08-02: Updated retrospective items and added autoscaler action (Samir Patel, reviewed by Ava Martinez).

If you are on-call and uncertain about the next step: page the secondary on-call immediately and follow the runbook checklist above.
